Petroleos de Venezuela SA Announces Major Investment to Boost Output

CARACAS, June 13 – Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) said Thursday it will invest $1.2 billion in upgrades across several key oilfields, aiming to increase crude production and modernize infrastructure in the Orinoco Belt and western Zulia state.

The company said the investment, to be rolled out over the next 18 months, will focus on rehabilitating drilling rigs, upgrading pipeline networks, and improving storage facilities. PDVSA expects these initiatives to add around 120,000 barrels per day to the country's current output by mid-2025.

"These projects are part of our commitment to revive Venezuela's energy sector and ensure stable supplies to our domestic and international partners," said PDVSA President Rafael Tellez in a statement. "By investing in technology and our workforce, we are laying the groundwork for sustained growth."

Venezuela, home to the world’s largest proven oil reserves, has seen oil production gradually rise this year, reaching nearly 900,000 barrels per day in May according to official figures. Industry analysts say the new investment could help the country consolidate recent gains.

"It’s a significant move," said energy consultant Maria Gutierrez of Caracas-based Velar Energy Advisors. "Rehabilitating equipment and infrastructure is essential if Venezuela wants to regain its standing as a leading oil exporter. Much of the equipment in these areas is outdated, so this should help improve both output and reliability."

The planned upgrades include the installation of new pumps and enhanced automation in the Jose processing complex, as well as expanded training for technical staff. PDVSA said local suppliers such as OilServ Venezuela and Energía Llanera will play a role in delivering the projects.

Union leaders welcomed the announcement, saying it could secure thousands of jobs. "This investment will have a positive impact on our communities and workers," said Jorge Rivas, head of the Petroleum Workers Federation. "We look forward to ongoing dialogue with management as the projects move ahead."

PDVSA said it will continue to evaluate additional expansion opportunities in other basins. The company reiterated its commitment to environmental standards and local economic development as it implements the upgrades.
